description: Creates or cancels spot instance requests.

parameters.name: access_key
parameters.description: AWS access key ID. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID or AWS_ACCESS_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The aws_access_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_access_key_id alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: aws_ca_bundle
parameters.description: The location of a CA Bundle to use when validating SSL certificates. The AWS_CA_BUNDLE environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: aws_config
parameters.description: A dictionary to modify the botocore configuration. Parameters can be found in the AWS documentation https://botocore.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/reference/config.html#botocore.config.Config.

parameters.name: client_token
parameters.description: The idempotency token you provided when you launched the instance, if applicable.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of instances to launch. Default: 1

parameters.name: debug_botocore_endpoint_logs
parameters.description: Use a botocore.endpoint logger to parse the unique (rather than total) "resource:action" API calls made during a task, outputing the set to the resource_actions key in the task results. Use the aws_resource_action callback to output to total list made during a playbook. The ANSIBLE_DEBUG_BOTOCORE_LOGS environment variable may also be used. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: endpoint_url
parameters.description: URL to connect to instead of the default AWS endpoints. While this can be used to connection to other AWS-compatible services the amazon.aws and community.aws collections are only tested against AWS. The AWS_URL environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: interruption
parameters.description: The behavior when a Spot Instance is interrupted. Choices: "hibernate" "stop" "terminate" ← (default)

parameters.name: launch_group
parameters.description: Launch group for spot requests, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/how-spot-instances-work.html#spot-launch-group.

parameters.name: launch_specification
parameters.description: The launch specification.

parameters.name: block_device_mappings
parameters.description: A list of hash/dictionaries of volumes to add to the new instance.

parameters.name: device_name
parameters.description: The device name (for example, /dev/sdh or xvdh).

parameters.name: ebs
parameters.description: Parameters used to automatically set up EBS volumes when the instance is launched, see https://boto3.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/reference/services/ec2.html#EC2.Client.request_spot_instances.

parameters.name: no_device
parameters.description: To omit the device from the block device mapping, specify an empty string.

parameters.name: virtual_name
parameters.description: The virtual device name

parameters.name: ebs_optimized
parameters.description: Whether instance is using optimized EBS volumes, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/EBSOptimized.html. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: iam_instance_profile
parameters.description: The IAM instance profile.

parameters.name: arn
parameters.description: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the instance profile. Only one of launch_specification.iam_instance_profile.arn or launch_specification.iam_instance_profile.name may be specified.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the instance profile. Only one of launch_specification.iam_instance_profile.arn or launch_specification.iam_instance_profile.name may be specified.

parameters.name: image_id
parameters.description: The ID of the AMI.

parameters.name: instance_type
parameters.description: Instance type to use for the instance, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/instance-types.html. Required when creating a new instance.

parameters.name: kernel_id
parameters.description: The ID of the kernel.

parameters.name: key_name
parameters.description: Key to use on the instance. The SSH key must already exist in AWS in order to use this argument. Keys can be created / deleted using the amazon.aws.ec2_key module.

parameters.name: monitoring
parameters.description: Indicates whether basic or detailed monitoring is enabled for the instance.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: Indicates whether detailed monitoring is enabled. Otherwise, basic monitoring is enabled. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: network_interfaces
parameters.description: One or more network interfaces. If you specify a network interface, you must specify subnet IDs and security group IDs using the network interface. Default: []

parameters.name: associate_carrier_ip_address
parameters.description: Indicates whether to assign a carrier IP address to the network interface. Choices: false true

parameters.name: associate_public_ip_address
parameters.description: Indicates whether to assign a public IPv4 address to an instance you launch in a VPC. Choices: false true

parameters.name: delete_on_termination
parameters.description: If set to true , the interface is deleted when the instance is terminated. You can specify true only if creating a new network interface when launching an instance. Choices: false true

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: The description of the network interface. Applies only if creating a network interface when launching an instance.

parameters.name: device_index
parameters.description: The position of the network interface in the attachment order. A primary network interface has a device index of 0. If you specify a network interface when launching an instance, you must specify the device index.

parameters.name: groups
parameters.description: The IDs of the security groups for the network interface. Applies only if creating a network interface when launching an instance.

parameters.name: interface_type
parameters.description: The type of network interface. Choices: "interface" "efa"

parameters.name: ipv4_prefix_count
parameters.description: The number of IPv4 delegated prefixes to be automatically assigned to the network interface

parameters.name: ipv4_prefixes
parameters.description: One or more IPv4 delegated prefixes to be assigned to the network interface.

parameters.name: ipv6_address_count
parameters.description: A number of IPv6 addresses to assign to the network interface

parameters.name: ipv6_addresses
parameters.description: One or more IPv6 addresses to assign to the network interface.

parameters.name: ipv6address
parameters.description: The IPv6 address.

parameters.name: ipv6_prefix_count
parameters.description: The number of IPv6 delegated prefixes to be automatically assigned to the network interface

parameters.name: ipv6_prefixes
parameters.description: One or more IPv6 delegated prefixes to be assigned to the network interface

parameters.name: network_card_index
parameters.description: The index of the network card.

parameters.name: network_interface_id
parameters.description: The ID of the network interface.

parameters.name: private_ip_address
parameters.description: The private IPv4 address of the network interface

parameters.name: private_ip_addresses
parameters.description: One or more private IPv4 addresses to assign to the network interface

parameters.name: secondary_private_ip_address_count
parameters.description: The number of secondary private IPv4 addresses.

parameters.name: subnet_id
parameters.description: The ID of the subnet associated with the network interface

parameters.name: placement
parameters.description: The placement information for the instance.

parameters.name: availability_zone
parameters.description: The Availability Zone.

parameters.name: group_name
parameters.description: The name of the placement group.

parameters.name: tenancy
parameters.description: the tenancy of the host Choices: "default" ← (default) "dedicated" "host"

parameters.name: ramdisk_id
parameters.description: The ID of the RAM disk.

parameters.name: security_group_ids
parameters.description: Security group id (or list of ids) to use with the instance.

parameters.name: security_groups
parameters.description: Security group name (or list of group names) to use with the instance. Only supported with EC2 Classic. To launch in a VPC, use launch_specification.security_group_ids.

parameters.name: user_data
parameters.description: The base64-encoded user data for the instance. User data is limited to 16 KB.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: A named AWS profile to use for authentication. See the AWS documentation for more information about named profiles https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-profiles.html. The AWS_PROFILE environment variable may also be used. The profile option is mutually exclusive with the aws_access_key, aws_secret_key and session_token options.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The AWS region to use. For global services such as IAM, Route53 and CloudFront, region is ignored. The AWS_REGION environment variable may also be used. See the Amazon AWS documentation for more information http://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#ec2_region.

parameters.name: secret_key
parameters.description: AWS secret access key. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY or AWS_SECRET_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The secret_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_secret_access_key alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: session_token
parameters.description: AWS STS session token for use with temporary credentials. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SESSION_TOKEN environment variable may also be used. The session_token and profile options are mutually exclusive.

parameters.name: spot_instance_request_ids
parameters.description: List of strings with IDs of spot requests to be cancelled

parameters.name: spot_price
parameters.description: Maximum spot price to bid. If not set, a regular on-demand instance is requested. A spot request is made with this maximum bid. When it is filled, the instance is started.

parameters.name: spot_type
parameters.description: The type of spot request. After being interrupted a persistent spot instance will be started once there is capacity to fill the request again. Choices: "one-time" ← (default) "persistent"

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Whether the spot request should be created or removed. When state=present, launch_specification is required. When state=absent, spot_instance_request_ids is required. Choices: "absent" "present" ← (default)

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: A dictionary of key-value pairs for tagging the Spot Instance request on creation.

parameters.name: terminate_instances
parameters.description: Boolean value to set whether or not to terminate instances associated to spot request. Can be used only when state=absent. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: validate_certs
parameters.description: When set to false, SSL certificates will not be validated for communication with the AWS APIs. Setting validate_certs=false is strongly discouraged, as an alternative, consider setting aws_ca_bundle instead. Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: zone_group
parameters.description: Name for logical grouping of spot requests. All spot instances in the request are launched in the same availability zone.

examples:
# Note: These examples do not set authentication details, see the AWS Guide for details.

- name: Simple Spot Request Creation
  amazon.aws.ec2_spot_instance:
    launch_specification:
      image_id: ami-123456789
      key_name: my-keypair
      instance_type: t2.medium

- name: Spot Request Creation with more options
  amazon.aws.ec2_spot_instance:
    launch_specification:
      image_id: ami-123456789
      key_name: my-keypair
      instance_type: t2.medium
      subnet_id: subnet-12345678
      block_device_mappings:
        - device_name: /dev/sdb
          ebs:
            delete_on_termination: true
            volume_type: gp3
            volume_size: 5
        - device_name: /dev/sdc
          ebs:
            delete_on_termination: true
            volume_type: io2
            volume_size: 30
      network_interfaces:
        - associate_public_ip_address: false
          delete_on_termination: true
          device_index: 0
      placement:
        availability_zone: us-west-2a
      monitoring:
        enabled: false
    spot_price: 0.002
    tags:
      Environment: Testing

- name: Spot Request Termination
  amazon.aws.ec2_spot_instance:
    spot_instance_request_ids: ['sir-12345678', 'sir-abcdefgh']
    state: absent

return_values.name: cancelled_spot_request
return_values.description: Details of the cancelled spot instance request. Returned: when cancellation is successful Sample: "Spot requests with IDs: sir-1234abcd have been cancelled"

return_values.name: spot_request
return_values.description: The spot instance request details after creation.
